chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me, saying: Abu Sa'id Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Zakariyya Al-'Adawi Al-Basri narrated to me from Haytham ibn 'Abdillah Al-Rummani, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu 'Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: The days of those who perform the Ziyarah of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) are not counted as part of their lifespans, nor are they deducted from their appointed term (of life).
ai.seo_question: What happens to the lifespan of those who visit Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Imam Al-Sadiq (a.s.) declares that the duration of visiting Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.) is excluded from one's lifespan, a concept known as 'Ziyarat is not counted from life.' This signifies that such devotion is a divine grace that extends one's spiritual existence rather than consuming it, reflecting the high status of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia eschatology. The narration underscores the transformative power of pilgrimage, where time spent in reverence is rewarded with added life or preserved for the Hereafter.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from Abī Sa’īd Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Zakariyyā Al-‘Adawi Al-Basri, from Haytham ibn ‘Abdillāh Al-Rummāni, from Abil Ḥasan (Imam Riďā (a.s.)), from his father (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)), who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh, Ja’far ibn Muḥammad Al-Sādiq (a.s.) said: The days spent by those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) are not counted as part of their lives; they do not reduce from their time (to death).
